description:
The reconcile-docs-from-spec-gap-analysis TODO was scoped to docs-only
edits; verification of those doc edits against benchbox/ surfaced three
code-level inconsistencies that were flagged but not fixed. Each is a
small, independent cleanup. None are user-visible today - all would
surface only if a user trusted the "wrong" source of truth (a Literal
type, a helper predicate, or a code pattern) and hit the divergence.

**C1 - datavault hash algorithm type vs runtime contract.**
`benchbox/core/datavault/etl/hash_functions.py:16` declares
`HashAlgorithm = Literal["md5", "sha1", "sha256"]`, but
`benchbox/core/datavault/benchmark.py:56` pins
`SUPPORTED_HASH_ALGORITHMS = ("md5",)` and the validator at L89-92
raises ValueError on anything else. The error message explains the
cause ("schema constraints"), so the fix is to narrow the Literal to
match runtime - not widen the allowlist.

**C2 - DuckDB ACL classification disagrees between two sources.**
`benchbox/core/metadata_primitives/ddl.py:583` defines
`no_acl = {"sqlite", "datafusion", "spark", "polars"}`, so
`supports_acl("duckdb")` returns True. But the authoritative tier
legend in `benchbox/core/metadata_primitives/catalog/queries.yaml:1435-1438`
lists DuckDB in Tier 4 (None - no SQL-level ACL support), and the four
other `supports_*` predicates (introspection, role_hierarchy,
column_grants) all return False for DuckDB. Pick one authoritative
source: either add `"duckdb"` to the `no_acl` set or update the yaml
legend + metadata-primitives.md to match the predicate. The yaml is
more consistent with reality (DuckDB is embedded, single-user, no
practical GRANT/REVOKE), so adding `"duckdb"` to `no_acl` is the
preferred direction.

**N1 - throughput stream cursor helper inconsistently adopted.**
`benchbox/platforms/base/execution.py` has five throughput paths that
call `connection.cursor()` directly (lines 547, 673, 765, 854, 1534)
and one (line 369) that uses the `_make_stream_cursor` wrapper. The
wrapper falls back to `_NoCloseProxy` for connection types that don't
implement `.cursor()`, so the direct-call paths will break for such
adapters. Standardise on `_make_stream_cursor` across all six.

anti_patterns.instead: only the no_acl set needs 'duckdb' added
just adopt the helper at the five call sites
anti_patterns.why: the proxy is load-bearing for adapters without .cursor()
the schema uses fixed-width BINARY(16) columns sized for MD5 and the error message explicitly cites 'schema constraints'

preserves.behavior: All five throughput paths in execution.py continue to produce an object with a .execute() method (the _NoCloseProxy fallback preserves this for non-cursor-capable connections)
DataVaultBenchmark hash validation continues to reject sha1/sha256 with the existing error message at benchmark.py:89-92
supports_acl_introspection/role_hierarchy/column_grants predicates unchanged - only the no_acl set in supports_acl changes
